verification_note: Verified on Windows 11 x86_64-pc-windows-msvc and on Linux x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu (WSL2, Ubuntu 26.04 LTS), both with Rust 1.98.1. The Linux run executed the full gate suite: fmt, clippy pedantic with -D warnings, 954 tests, rustdoc with -D warnings, the tools workspace, and all four policy gates. macOS is recorded as 'unverified': no macOS host is reachable from the machine that produced this registry, so marking it would be a claim with nothing behind it. Every 'complete' entry was re-checked against the file it cites; the thirteen citations that did not survive that check were corrected rather than left standing.

features.summary: Windowed access to large collections: a viewport over a million records costs the same as a viewport over a thousand, because the window is computed from the measured rows rather than from the collection.

unit_tests.evidence: crates/ncui-state/src/virtualize.rs — a_window_ignores_the_size_of_the_collection_it_is_a_window_into (a million-record window covers as many indices as a thousand-record one), a_uniform_window_covers_the_same_rows_at_any_collection_size, and a_window_over_unmeasured_records_is_estimated_not_invented

failure_tests.evidence: crates/ncui-state/src/virtualize.rs — measuring_zero_removes_the_measurement, setting_a_smaller_total_drops_measurements_past_the_end, and an_unknown_total_produces_no_window_rather_than_a_guess

benchmarks.evidence: crates/ncui-state/src/virtualize.rs — the work bound is checked from two directions. a_window_ignores_the_size_of_the_collection_it_is_a_window_into bounds the inspected indices; a_walk_of_every_record_is_caught_even_if_the_counter_is_not_touched bounds wall-clock time at a deep offset, because a self-reported counter is gameable by code that simply does not increment it. Measured by running mutations against the suite: an O(n) index_at and an overscan scaled by the collection size are both caught. Four shapes are NOT caught, recorded here rather than left for a reader to discover — an early-returning O(n) walk, a walk worse than linear in the measured count, redundant work inside one pass that charges no counter, and a fixed constant-factor slowdown. The first two are linear-growth or faster and sit inside the timing bounds; the last two are constant factors that a ratio cannot see. Closing them means instrumenting rather than thresholding, or pinning an absolute cost per operation.

tracing.evidence: crates/ncui-state/src/virtualize.rs — accessors over stored state: it defines the stable labels and counters the runtime increments rather than incrementing any itself. The previous citation claimed this file emits the metric

metrics.evidence: crates/ncui-state/src/virtualize.rs — accessors over stored state: it defines the stable labels and counters the runtime increments rather than incrementing any itself. The previous citation claimed this file emits the metric

documentation.evidence: crates/ncui-state/src/virtualize.rs — the module documentation states the cost is O(m) in the measured count and explicitly corrects an earlier claim of O(log m), which is what this slot previously cited. The registry recorded the retracted claim

security_review.evidence: crates/ncui-state/src/virtualize.rs — the module performs no I/O, reads no user input and holds no item data; the only inputs are a count, an offset and measured heights, and a non-finite or negative height is refused rather than allowed to corrupt the offset arithmetic
